source: Krieglstein, Beege et al. (2022) A systematic meta-analysis of the reliability and validity of subjective cognitive load questionnaires
finding: Germane load questionnaire scales are internally consistent. The GCL scale is the most reliable of the three.
numbers: Pooled Cronbach alpha: ICL .823, ECL .773, GCL .860 (GCL k=42). No publication bias on alpha. Four questionnaires (Leppink 2013, Klepsch 2017, Leppink 2014, Eysink 2009).
limits: High alpha shows items agree with each other, not that they measure germane processing. Eysink scale uses single items for ICL and GCL.
agent_relevance: A germane score from self-report is stable but does not prove it tracks schema building. Do not use a self-rated effort as a proxy for useful thinking in the agent.

source: Krieglstein, Beege et al. (2022) A systematic meta-analysis of the reliability and validity of subjective cognitive load questionnaires
finding: Germane load correlates with learning, but only weakly, and only for the Leppink and Klepsch scales.
numbers: Leppink 2013 scale: GCL-retention r=.188 (k=15, p<.001), GCL-transfer r=.173 (k=12, p<.001). Klepsch 2017 scale: GCL-retention r=.219 (k=7), GCL-transfer r=.217 (k=6). Compare ECL-retention r=-.114 for Leppink.
limits: r near .2 means about 4% of variance. Leppink 2014 scale: GCL did not correlate with retention (r=-.008, k=2, ns). Eysink 2009 single-item scale: GCL correlated NEGATIVELY with retention (r=-.223, k=9) and transfer (r=-.182, k=9).
agent_relevance: Germane effort predicts learning only slightly, and the sign flips with the instrument. Treat more reasoning effort as unproven to help; test it per task.

source: Krieglstein, Beege et al. (2022) A systematic meta-analysis of the reliability and validity of subjective cognitive load questionnaires
finding: Germane load is not well separated from intrinsic load in ratings. ICL and GCL correlate strongly and positively.
numbers: Leppink 2013: ICL-GCL r=.403 (k=19, p<.001); ECL-GCL r=-.086 (k=20, ns); ICL-ECL r=.298 (k=25). Klepsch 2017: ICL-GCL r=.533 (k=10); ECL-GCL r=-.246 (k=10, p=.045); ICL-ECL r=.350 (k=16).
limits: Theory says ECL and GCL should be negatively related. This held weakly (Klepsch) or not at all (Leppink). Authors still conclude results favour the three-factor model.
agent_relevance: Hard task content drives both intrinsic and germane scores. In the agent, task difficulty and useful schema effort will be confounded unless varied independently.

source: Krieglstein, Beege et al. (2022) A systematic meta-analysis of the reliability and validity of subjective cognitive load questionnaires
finding: Germane load shows no link to prior knowledge, while intrinsic and extraneous load fall as prior knowledge rises.
numbers: GCL-prior knowledge: Leppink 2013 r=.073 (k=15, ns), Klepsch 2017 r=.014 (k=9, ns). Eysink 2009: r=-.193 (k=6, p=.024). ICL and ECL correlated negatively with prior knowledge.
limits: Contradicts a simple story that experts invest more germane effort. It fits Sweller 2023's claim that germane load is not an independent load.
agent_relevance: No reason to scale a schema-building budget with how much the agent already knows; the data do not show that pattern.

source: Leutner & Biele (2025) Without integration, everything is nothing: meta-analysis of instructional support for drawing-to-learn
finding: Supports meant to raise germane load did not improve learning from drawing. Supports that force integration did.
numbers: 14 studies, 16 comparisons, N=1213. Overall support effect on comprehension g=0.04 (SE .11, p=.738; N=590 vs 623); transfer g=-0.10 (k=7, p=.696). Moderator increase germane load: Q(1)=0.92, p=.339 (ns). Moderator reduce extraneous load: Q(1)=0.00, p=.976. Moderator facilitates integration: Q(1)=7.90, p=.005; g=0.35 with it, g=-0.15 without.
quote: drawing support that could be expected to facilitate the integration process significantly increased students' comprehension (g=0.35)
limits: Small k; transfer could not be tested for moderators (k=7 < 10). Coding of germane versus integration was by the authors and overlaps. Drawing only, mostly science text.
agent_relevance: Not all extra generative work helps. What helped was making the learner join separate representations into one model. In the schema, prefer an explicit integrate step over a generic think-harder step.

source: Sweller, van Merrienboer & Paas (2019) Cognitive architecture and instructional design: 20 years later
finding: Germane load was redefined: it is no longer extra load that adds to the total. It is working memory redirected from extraneous to intrinsic activity.
numbers: 1998 version: germane substitutes for extraneous load. 2019 version: germane load redistributes resources. Reason given: studies showed total load FALLS when extraneous load is cut, which the 1998 substitution idea could not allow.
quote: germane cognitive load redistributes working memory resources from extraneous activities to activities directly relevant to learning
limits: Redefinition protects the theory from the substitution problem but makes germane load unfalsifiable as a separate quantity.
agent_relevance: For the agent, only two things need design: cut extraneous tokens and set intrinsic difficulty. Germane is the result, not a dial.

source: Sweller, van Merrienboer & Paas (2019) Cognitive architecture and instructional design: 20 years later
finding: The founding germane-load evidence was the variability effect (Paas and van Merrienboer 1994). It depended on the load level of the task.
numbers: Prediction: high-variability practice helps transfer with worked examples (low load) and hurts with conventional problem solving (high load). The interaction between problem format and variability was found.
limits: The 2019 review gives the result in words, not exact means. Study used geometry problems. Load interpretation is post hoc (see de Jong 2010).
agent_relevance: Variety in practice items is worth adding only when each item is cheap to process. With a heavy task, vary less.

source: Sweller, van Merrienboer & Paas (2019) Cognitive architecture and instructional design: 20 years later
finding: Self-explanation prompts and imagination instructions raise learning only if total load stays within capacity and the learner has enough knowledge.
numbers: Self-explanation prompts on worked examples beat worked examples without prompts provided total load does not exceed capacity. Imagination beats study only after enough expertise; before that, study is better (Cooper et al. 2001).
limits: Boundary conditions stated by the authors, no pooled effect sizes in this review.
agent_relevance: Gate generative steps (explain, imagine, compare) on task state: use them after the solution is understood, not while it is still being worked out.

source: Sweller (2023) The development of cognitive load theory: replication crises and incorporation of other theories
finding: Sweller states there are no germane load effects. The idea was never built from data.
numbers: Extraneous effects: many. Intrinsic effects: several. Germane effects: none generated in 25 years.
quote: there were no germane cognitive load effects being generated
limits: The author is a founder of the theory, so this is a self-correction, not an outside test. Statement is narrative, no counts.
agent_relevance: Germane load is a design hypothesis, not a result. Do not cite it as support for a scaffold step.

source: Sweller (2023) The development of cognitive load theory: replication crises and incorporation of other theories
finding: Failed replications drove the theory: worked examples failed with geometry and kinematics but worked with algebra; split attention failed with self-sufficient text and diagram, giving the redundancy effect.
numbers: Chandler and Sweller 1991: integrating blood-flow diagram and text gave no advantage; dropping the text did better.
limits: Account is by the original authors. They call these conceptual replication failures that exposed moderators (element interactivity, expertise).
agent_relevance: A scaffold step that helps on one task type may fail on another. Moderator checks must be built into tests of every step.

source: de Jong (2010) Cognitive load theory, educational research, and instructional design: some food for thought
finding: Germane load as used in the founding evidence is a post hoc label. Higher load plus better transfer was called germane after the fact.
numbers: Variability: higher rated load and better transfer was read as germane. de Croock et al. (1998) distillery troubleshooting: high variability gave better transfer without higher rated load.
quote: Apart from the fact that this is a post-hoc explanation there seem to be no grounds for asserting
limits: Critique of reasoning, not a new experiment. The de Croock result is one study.
agent_relevance: Same risk in agent logs: if extra reasoning tokens go with better answers, that does not show the tokens were germane. Needs ablation.

source: de Jong (2010) Cognitive load theory, educational research, and instructional design: some food for thought
finding: Germane load can overload. A good process can still exceed working memory, and nobody can state where that line is.
numbers: Stull and Mayer (2007): students who built graphic organisers themselves did worse than students given author-made organisers.
limits: Interpretation open: authors blamed extraneous load, de Jong suggests too-demanding germane work. No way to tell them apart in the data.
agent_relevance: Asking the agent to generate its own structure (outline, schema) can cost more than receiving one. Compare generate versus provide.

source: de Jong (2010) Cognitive load theory, educational research, and instructional design: some food for thought
finding: Whether a load is germane or extraneous depends on learner expertise and goal, so the split is not fixed by the task.
numbers: Quotes Paas et al. (2004): germane for a novice may be extraneous for an expert. Gerjets and Scheiter (2003): goal-dependent effect.
limits: Links germane load to the expertise-reversal effect (covered in subfield 04).
agent_relevance: The same prompt step should be switched on or off by state: novel problem versus familiar problem.

source: Kalyuga (2011) Cognitive load theory: how many types of load does it really need?
finding: Kalyuga argues germane load is redundant with intrinsic load. Only the dual intrinsic/extraneous model is needed.
numbers: No numbers. Germane load was added on theory grounds, not to explain data. Learning activities always needed methods from outside the theory.
limits: Only the Springer abstract page was available (full text paywalled), so detail is from the abstract.
agent_relevance: Supports dropping a separate germane module in the schema.

source: Sweller (2010) Element interactivity and intrinsic, extraneous, and germane cognitive load
finding: Sweller proposes germane load be defined as working memory resources actually used on intrinsic (not extraneous) load.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Only the Springer abstract page was available.
agent_relevance: Same as Sweller 2019 redefinition; treat germane as allocation, not an input.

source: Klepsch, Schmitz & Seufert (2017) Development and validation of two instruments measuring intrinsic, extraneous, and germane cognitive load
finding: Naive-rating questionnaires could separate three load types after items were rewritten. Germane load was the weakest scale.
numbers: Study 1 N=97 (informed n=48, naive n=49): naive GCL did not separate low and high GCL tasks, F(1,88)=0.04, p=.84. Study 2 (65-95 per task, 17 tasks): GCL 3 items alpha=.67, 2 items alpha=.85; task discrimination d=.35 versus ICL d=.73 and ECL d=.94.
quote: the three-partite model seems to be more adequate
limits: Germane effect on ratings is half or less that of the other two. Tasks were hypothetical or short. Study 1 informed rating alpha only .25.
agent_relevance: Even with tuned items the germane signal is small. Do not rely on it as an agent signal.

source: Klepsch, Schmitz & Seufert (2017) Development and validation of two instruments measuring intrinsic, extraneous, and germane cognitive load
finding: Multi-group CFA preferred a three-factor load model, but a two-factor model fit almost as well.
numbers: One factor: chi2(238)=1709.15, CFI .612, RMSEA .071, AIC 2185. Three factors: chi2(221)=335.11, CFI .970, TLI .951, RMSEA .021, AIC 845. Two factors: chi2(187)=283.89, CFI .974, RMSEA .021, AIC 862.
limits: AIC differences are small between 2 and 3 factors; CFI is slightly higher for the two-factor model.
agent_relevance: Statistics cannot settle the three-versus-two load question.

source: Jiang & Kalyuga (2020) Confirmatory factor analysis of cognitive load ratings supports a two-factor model
finding: Confirmatory factor analysis of a 12-item rating set fit a two-factor (intrinsic, extraneous) model. Germane items were treated as extra intrinsic items.
numbers: N=60 first-year English-as-a-foreign-language students. chi2=54.069, df=53, p=.433; CFI .994; TLI .993; RMSEA .018; SRMR .077. Alpha .78. One item loaded .28.
limits: Small sample, one task (listening), reverse-coded germane items. Did not test a three-factor model against the two-factor one.
agent_relevance: Fits the view that germane is not needed as a separate construct. Weak evidence by itself.

source: Debue & Van de Leemput (2014) What does germane load mean? An empirical contribution to the cognitive load theory
finding: Germane-load ratings did not predict performance. They tracked immersion and enjoyment.
numbers: N=128 (phase 1 n=92: text+pictures+animations n=30, text+pictures n=32, text only n=30). GL-performance r=.045 (ns). GL-focused immersion r=.362, GL-enjoyment r=.401, GL-temporal dissociation r=.289 (all p<.01). EL-GL r=-.470. Performance differed by version, F(2,91)=5.605, eta2=.112, but GL did not.
quote: Results showed the expected opposite relationships between germane and extraneous load
limits: Phase 2 eye tracking had about 24 usable participants and nearly nothing significant. One-time rating at end of task.
agent_relevance: Feeling absorbed is not the same as schema building. An agent-side engagement signal could mislead.

source: Skulmowski & Xu (2022) Understanding cognitive load in digital and online learning: a new perspective on extraneous cognitive load
finding: Cost-benefit view: some extraneous load buys germane processing, so cutting all extraneous load is not always best.
numbers: Two mechanisms proposed: (1) pay a little perceptual extraneous load to gain germane processing; (2) the same information is extraneous for experts and intrinsic for novices. Example: learning to tell relevant from irrelevant information is itself part of the task (information reduction hypothesis).
limits: Conceptual review, no pooled effect. Notes Mayer (2014): motivating but extra material can raise generative processing.
agent_relevance: Do not strip every extra token or distractor from agent context by default. Test it: some noise may be a useful training signal.

source: Skulmowski & Xu (2022) Understanding cognitive load in digital and online learning: a new perspective on extraneous cognitive load
finding: The 2019 model removes germane load from the additive total. Authors keep germane processing as a separate benefit dimension.
numbers: Model: total load = intrinsic + extraneous; germane processing is the benefit side, tied to motivation and engagement in much of the literature.
limits: Conceptual. Authors note interest from design features does not always give better learning (Pedra et al. 2015).
agent_relevance: Track cost (tokens, context) and benefit (verified progress) separately instead of adding them.

source: Adapala (2025) Cognitive load limits in large language models: benchmarking multi-hop reasoning
finding: Extraneous load (irrelevant filler) lowers multi-hop accuracy for the one model that was above floor; three models scored zero even on clean input.
numbers: 200 questions (50 SEC filings, 100 FanOutQA, 50 MINTQA), 10 replications per condition, 5 models. Gemini-2.0-Flash EM: control .85, long control .82, 20% load .82, 50% .78, 80% .72; slope -0.003 per % load (95% CI -.004 to -.002, p<.001); hop recall .90 to .75. GPT-4o-0613: control .65, 80% load .55, slope -0.002 (p=.07); 32% of outputs lacked a final answer before mitigation, 12% after. Llama-3-8B, Llama-3-70B, Mistral-7B: 0.00 everywhere.
quote: Germane Load represents the effort for meaningful computation
limits: Only Gemini gives an interpretable load effect. Single-item load measures. Three datasets. Germane load was NOT measured; the paper only labels it effort for meaningful computation.
agent_relevance: Irrelevant context costs accuracy, about 13 points at 80% filler for the capable model. This supports pruning context, not any germane step.

source: Gupta, Liu & Zou (2026) Extraneous cognitive load in large language models (NeurIPS 2026 poster)
finding: A benchmark varying five presentation factors finds higher extraneous load often lowers LLM accuracy. Steering activations toward low-load directions improves performance.
numbers: Benchmark CogLoadBench: five presentation factors, three reasoning task families. An activation-based Extraneous Load Score is proposed. Page gives no accuracy numbers or model names.
limits: Only the poster abstract was read, not the paper. Germane load is not part of the study.
agent_relevance: Evidence that presentation load matters for LLMs is growing. Still on extraneous load only.

source: Zhang (2025) Cognitive load-aware inference: a neuro-symbolic framework for optimizing the token economy of LLMs
finding: A prompt framework maps intrinsic, extraneous and germane load to LLM steps and reports about 35% fewer tokens at equal accuracy. Results are unreplicated.
numbers: CLAI-Prompt vs standard CoT, Llama-3-70B: GSM8K 92.3 vs 92.5 acc, tokens 310 vs 485 (-36.1%); MATH 53.5 vs 53.9, tokens 525 vs 812 (-35.3%). LongBench QA (Llama-3-8B): F1 69.3, 980 tokens (4.2x compression) vs LLMLingua 68.1 and full context 65.2. Fine-tuned CLAI-Tune (Llama-3-8B-Instruct): GSM8K 91.5, 255 tokens (-43.3%).
limits: Single author, preprint, no seeds or confidence intervals, no ablation of the germane stage versus the sub-question and context-cleaning stages. Cannot tell if the gain comes from germane-style steps or from plain decomposition and brevity.
agent_relevance: The token saving is plausible from brevity and decomposition. It is not evidence that a germane step helps. Ablation needed before copying.

source: Krieglstein, Beege et al. (2022) A systematic meta-analysis of the reliability and validity of subjective cognitive load questionnaires
finding: Reliability of load scales did not depend on setting, domain or presentation, except interactive media lowered GCL reliability.
numbers: GCL alpha by domain: natural sciences .872 (k=30), social sciences .869, logic and mathematics .795 (k=5). Presentation: static .866, dynamic .884, interactive .774 (k=6). Alpha by response points: 7-point .732 (k=12), 11-point .915 (k=16).
limits: Few studies in maths and interactive cells. Scale length confounds with questionnaire used.
agent_relevance: Scale choice alone moves GCL reliability from .73 to .92, so any germane score in an agent audit should come from one fixed instrument.

source: Sweller (2023) The development of cognitive load theory: replication crises and incorporation of other theories
finding: Sweller argues cognitive load effects were refined by failed replications, and effects depend on element interactivity and learner expertise.
numbers: Worked example effect not found for geometry and kinematics problems in early work, found for algebra. Split-attention integration gave no gain for self-sufficient diagram and text.
limits: No new replication data in this essay. Account of earlier, mostly unpublished or older failures.
agent_relevance: Include a moderator gate (task interactivity, prior knowledge) before any scaffold step that adds processing.

source: Krieglstein, Beege et al. (2022) A systematic meta-analysis of the reliability and validity of subjective cognitive load questionnaires
finding: Authors judge their pooled results as supporting the three-factor model, but note that the correlations among load types partly contradict theory.
numbers: Pooled data come from 4 instruments; Leppink 2014 and Eysink 2009 have few effect sizes (k=2 for some cells).
limits: Authors are on the measurement side; the conclusion is a reading of correlations, not a test against the two-factor model.
agent_relevance: Use as the pro-three-factor counterweight to Kalyuga 2011 and Jiang and Kalyuga 2020.
